findings.title: Incomplete Logout Implementation
findings.description: The logout function in lib/security/scanners/auth_scanner.dart does not appear to clear local authentication tokens or cache.
findings.risk: If local storage is not wiped during logout, another user or an attacker could potentially access the preceding session.
findings.recommendation: Ensure SharedPreferences, Hive boxes, and local caches are cleared or deleted when the user logs out.

findings.title: Potential Hardcoded Password or Auth Key
findings.description: Found variable assignment indicating a hardcoded password or token: "String deviceToken = 'deviceToken'"
findings.risk: Hardcoding passwords in code makes them accessible to any attacker who extracts the application binary.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve passwords dynamically from user input or encrypted vaults.

findings.title: WebView JavaScript Execution Enabled Unrestrictedly
findings.description: Detected a WebView instantiated with unrestricted JavaScript execution enabled.
findings.risk: Enabling JavaScript in WebViews allows loaded pages to execute code. If untrusted remote content is displayed, it could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks compromising local app data or bridge APIs.
findings.recommendation: Only enable JavaScript if strictly required. Ensure that navigation is restricted to HTTPS and approved domains using navigation delegates.

findings.title: Vulnerability Database Check Status
findings.description: Using built-in offline Dart/Flutter security rules database. Remote live vulnerability database check is not configured.
findings.risk: None. This is an informational message stating that live CVE lookup from OSV/GitHub Advisory is not active.
findings.recommendation: Periodically check dependencies using GitHub security alerts or running "dart pub token" or external tools.

findings.title: Potential StreamSubscription Memory Leak
findings.description: A stream listener was established in scratch/test_draft.dart, but no corresponding ".cancel()" call was detected in the file.
findings.risk: Active stream subscriptions retain references to listeners and context, which can keep widgets/controllers in memory forever if not canceled when no longer needed.
findings.recommendation: Store the StreamSubscription in a variable and call subscription.cancel() in dispose() or onClose().

findings.title: Potential Timer Memory Leak
findings.description: A Timer (or Timer.periodic) is created in lib/tools/runtime_perf_check/perf_dashboard_html.dart, but no ".cancel()" call was found.
findings.risk: Periodic timers keep running in the background and prevent garbage collection of their callback contexts, leading to memory and CPU leaks.

findings.title: Potential Memory Leak: Un-disposed TextEditingController
findings.description: A TextEditingController was created in templates/shared/common/reusable_component/dialogs/dispute_dialog.dart but there is no call to dispose() in the class.
findings.risk: Failing to dispose controllers leaves native observers and resources registered, causing severe memory leaks in the app.
findings.recommendation: Override the dispose() method in State or GetxController/BLoC and call controller.dispose().

findings.title: Use of Static ListView Instead of Lazy ListView.builder
findings.description: Using "ListView(children: ...)" instead of "ListView.builder(...)".
findings.risk: A standard ListView instantiates all children items at once, regardless of whether they are visible on screen, causing memory pressure and rendering delays for long lists.
findings.recommendation: Refactor to "ListView.builder(...)" to enable lazy-loading and item recycling for better scrolling performance.

findings.title: Controller Instantiation Inside Widget build() Method
findings.description: A controller is created inside the build() method of a widget in templates/shared/common/reusable_component/widgets/app_text_form_field.dart.
findings.risk: Controllers will be re-instantiated on every single widget build/rebuild, resetting their states and causing CPU spikes/memory leaks.
findings.recommendation: Convert the widget to a StatefulWidget and instantiate controllers in initState() and dispose them in dispose().
